# 1 Enoch Chapter 81 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**81:1** And he said to me: Observe, Enoch, these heavenly tablets, and read what is written thereon, and mark every individual fact.

**81:2** And I observed the heavenly tablets, and read everything which was written thereon and understood everything, and read the book of all the deeds of mankind, and of all the children of flesh that shall be upon the earth to the remotest generations.

**81:3** And forthwith I blessed the great Lord, the King of glory forever, in that He has made all the works of the world, and I praised the Lord because of His patience, and I blessed Him because of the children of men.

**81:4** And after that I said: Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness, concerning whom there is no book of unrighteousness written, and against whom no day of judgment shall be found.

**81:5** And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: Declare everything to your son Methuselah, and show to all your children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of the Lord, for He is their Creator.

**81:6** One year we will leave you with your son, until you give your last commands, that you may teach your children and record it for them, and testify to all your children; and in the second year they shall take you from their midst.

**81:7** Let your heart be strong, for the good shall announce righteousness to the good; the righteous with the righteous shall rejoice, and shall offer congratulation to one another.

**81:8** But the sinners shall die with the sinners, and the apostate shall sink down with the apostate.

**81:9** And those who practice righteousness shall die on account of the deeds of men, and be taken away on account of the doings of the godless.

**81:10** And in those days they ceased to speak to me, and I came to my people, blessing the Lord of the world.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus rendering adjudicated from EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA. Chapter 81 contains several theologically significant moments: (1) Enoch reads the heavenly tablets — complete history of all human deeds (v. 2); (2) The declaration "no flesh is righteous before the Lord" (v. 5) — a universally important theological statement anticipating similar formulations in Qumran texts and Paul; (3) Seven holy angels return Enoch to earth for one year to transmit the revelation to Methuselah. The 'book of unrighteousness' (v. 4) and 'day of judgment' are key eschatological terms.*
